reasons: UNSUPPORTED: "Roland Garros 'fue el torneo que más le costó'" (CNN only says it was the one Slam that eluded him. 'The one that cost him most' is the writer's own gloss, not stated by the source.)
UNSUPPORTED: "Söderling was 'verdugo de Nadal una semana antes'" (CNN says he knocked Nadal out 'earlier in the week', not a week before. Fix the wording or cite a source that gives the date.)

WRONG: "'Agassi, último campeón en París antes que él, le entregó el trofeo'" (CNN says Agassi was the 1999 French Open champion and the last player to win all four Slams. He was not the last Paris champion before Federer: Nadal won Roland Garros 2005-08. Correct to 'el último hombre en completar el Grand Slam de carrera' or 'campeón de 1999'.)

OUTDATED: "Foundation founded in 2003; 'ha llegado a más de un millón de niños y ha invertido más de 50 millones de dólares'; works in Zambia, Namibia, Zimbabwe, Malawi, Botswana, South Africa and Switzerland" (The ATP line matches, but the figures are old (the 1 million milestone was reached in 2018). ITHF's Federer page says more than three million children by early 2026, and the Wikipedia lead gives 3.82M by end of 2025 (a lead only). The sentence describes the present, so it needs a current figure from the foundation's own site or annual report. The foundation also appears to have been renamed 'Federer Foundation'.)
UNCITED: "'Roland Garros fue el torneo que más le costó' (interpretive; the next tagged sentence only supports that he had never won there)"
UNCITED: "'Sigue siendo aficionado del FC Basel' (present tense; the source line is undated)"

Reviewer recommends rejection: Almost every claim is confirmed against the sources, but two things must be fixed before publishing. (1) WRONG: 'Agassi, último campeón en París antes que él' contradicts CNN, which says Agassi won in 1999 and was the last man to complete the career Slam. Nadal won Paris in 2005-08. (2) OUTDATED: the foundation figures ('más de un millón de niños', '50 millones') are old. ITHF puts the reach at more than three million children by early 2026, so get the current figure and name from the foundation's own report. Also fix 'una semana antes' (Söderling over Nadal): CNN says 'earlier in the week'. Drop or soften 'el torneo que más le costó', which CNN does not say. Olympics.com could not be opened with web_fetch; its content was confirmed through the search result for the same URL.

claims.claim: Birth: 8 August 1981 in Basel, Switzerland (facts.birthDate, birthPlace, summary, FAQ, body)
claims.note: Britannica Quick Facts: born August 8, 1981, Basel. Nationality CH is consistent with Britannica and the ATP bio (Swiss father, Swiss tennis).

claims.claim: Age 45; turned 45 on 8 August 2026 (title, metaDescription, FAQ, intro)
claims.note: 1981-08-08 plus 45 years is 2026-08-08, so he is 45 on 2026-10-26. Olympics.com also calls him 'the 45-year-old'.

claims.claim: Ball boy at the Basel tournament in 1993 and 1994
claims.note: ATP bio: ballboy 1993-94 at his hometown tournament in Basel.

claims.claim: Retired in 2022 with 20 Grand Slam titles: 6 Australian Open, 1 Roland Garros, 8 Wimbledon, 5 US Open; pro career began in 1998
claims.note: Britannica Quick Facts: 20 singles Slams, split 6/1/8/5. Playing career 1998-2022.

claims.claim: Inducted into the Tennis Hall of Fame on Saturday 29 August 2026 in Newport, Rhode Island, aged 45, in his first year of eligibility; said fame was never the goal
claims.note: web_fetch of the Olympics.com URL failed (url_not_accessible). The search result for the same URL confirms Saturday 29 August, Newport, 45-year-old, first year of eligibility, record eight Wimbledon, and the 'fame was never the goal' quote. 29 Aug 2026 is a Saturday.

claims.claim: Parents (Robert Swiss, Lynette South African), sister Diana; began playing at 8; idols Edberg, Becker, Sampras; speaks English, French, German, Swiss German; supports FC Basel
claims.note: All in the ATP bio. 'Sigue siendo aficionado' (present tense) rests on a bio line with no date; minor.

claims.claim: Retirement letter: saw players as giants and began to dream as a ball kid; thanked Swiss Tennis for believing in him; thanked wife Mirka first
claims.note: Scroll full text confirms all three. Mirka is the first person thanked, after the announcement paragraphs.

claims.claim: Eight Wimbledon titles are a men's record; first man to reach 20 majors
claims.note: Olympics.com: record eight Wimbledon crowns. ITHF: first male player to win 20 major singles titles.

claims.claim: Records of 10 straight finals, 23 straight semifinals and 36 straight quarterfinals at Slams

Some paragraphs are dense ATP stat lists, but this is not padding.
